Timeline/1989
1989Journal article

Theory

The expressive power of a hidden layer

Under stated conditions, feedforward networks can approximate broad classes of functions.

Kurt Hornik, Maxwell Stinchcombe and Halbert White

AI topics

Explore related entries. Larger tags appear on more entries.

Neural networksLearning theoryComputation theory

The contribution

This theoretical work established approximation capabilities of multilayer feedforward networks. It helped explain why even a network with a single hidden layer, when given enough units and suitable assumptions, could represent a rich set of input-output relationships.

What this does not establish

Representational capacity does not guarantee that training finds the right weights, that the required network is small, or that predictions generalize.

Why this date?

1989 dates this particular universal-approximation paper; it is not a claim of sole priority for the theorem family.

This entry follows the linked publication. Read the source and date conventions.
